newsitem.title: SPAIN: SOCCER-WEEKEND FIXTURES IN THE SPANISH LEAGUE.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-WEEKEND FIXTURES IN THE SPANISH LEAGUE.

text.p: Games scheduled for the weekend in the Spanish league championship (league standings in parentheses, kick-off times GMT):
Dressing-room conflict has marred Real's preparations for the game with a clash between the Argentine Cesar Gomez and coach Javier Irureta, who looks set to pick midfielder Andoni Imaz.

Betis need to keep up the pressure on second-placed Barcelona against an Oviedo side which will be without Portuguese defender Abel Xavier, who will miss the game with knee problems. Leading goalscorer Oli Alvarez is also doubtful.

Sevilla traditionally do well in the Camp Nou and look set to bring back former Barcelona midfielder Robert Prosinecki. Anything but a win will not be enough for Barcelona, who are being pressurised for Spains's second European Cup place.
Logrones showed great spirit in last week's defeat by Barcelona and are one of 11 clubs involved in the relegation fight, while Valladolid are one of the other 11 still with UEFA Cup aspirations.
Athletic hope to keep their UEFA Cup challenge on course against a Compostela side where Juan Jose Viedma is the likely substitute for suspended defender Nacho Fernandez.

Extremadura have gone six home games without defeat, while Tenerife are one of the league's strongest teams away from home and are riding high after the midweek UEFA Cup quarter-final win over Brondby.

Real will be looking to consolidate their lead at the top of the league. There will be some interest in whether their three players on four yellow cards -- Predrag Mijatovic, Christian Panucci and Clarence Seedorf -- will deliberately pick up another so as to serve suspension when away on international duty.

Deportivo coach Carlos Alberto Silva will have to remodel his attack in the absence of injured Brazilian striker Renaldo but knows that a win will maintain his side's very real chances of ensuring a European Cup place for next season.
Hercules coach Quique Hernandez has to find replacements for suspended players Jose Lledo and Paquito Escudero and injured Yugoslav Josip Vinsjic for this vital relegation battle.
Maximo Hernandez will become the third Rayo coach to sit on the bench this season in the game against an Atletico side rocked by heroic defeats in both the European and Spanish Cup competitions.

Sporting will be without Russian midfielder Igor Lediakhov, who is suspended, and defender Nikiforov, who is injured. With Ariel Ortega at the helm, Valencia hope to find their way again after midweek UEFA Cup elimination.
